doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Pontiac childhood, family and piano training
title: Twelve years of study and later lessons in New York
summary: Twelve years with McCann in Pontiac, then lessons with Joe Postacoff and Yashir Zady while at CBS; classical study helps jazz.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: How long did this formal training continue?
Yeah. Well, yeah, in Pontiac. Then, when I left Pontiac, I took lessons from a different lady in New York.
This is when I was working at CBS as a concert pianist.
This is in the 70s. This is 30 years later.

That’s right. The lessons never stopped. I took lessons from this guy, Joe Postacoff in the Village for a time. But, Yashir Zady, I studied with him for several years. He knew all of the concert repertoire. He’s jazz player, this is classics. But, you see, you have to work on things like—I found that working on classics helped me to play jazz. The techniques involved when playing classical have to help you when you’re playing jazz. They help your facility. I think it improves you thinking, you know? It influences your thinking. Whatever degree, or whatever road you take, it influences it. You can think more clearly and more logically I believe.
